title: Your First Game
description: A sprite, an object, a room, and a player you move with the arrow keys.

title: Collect the Coins
description: Touch a coin to collect it, keep score, and show it on screen.

title: Blocks to Python
description: Build an event from blocks, read the Python they make, then turn it into Python.

title: Art from the Library
description: A walking hero from the free art library: two frames of a Kenney character, as a sprite.

title: A Tileset
description: A whole sheet of tiles from the library, and which of them are solid ground.

title: Painting a Room
description: A tile layer, a brush, a floor and a platform — and a second layer for the scenery.

title: Walking on Tiles
description: Gravity, solid ground, running and jumping, on the level you painted.

title: A Bigger World
description: A room wider than the screen, more ground to run on, a gap to fall through, and a camera that follows the hero.

title: 1. Hello, Python
description: Your first lines of Python: print messages to the Console, and leave notes in your code.

title: 2. Variables
description: Give a value a name, change it, and print it — how a program remembers a score, a name or a number of lives.

title: 3. Numbers and Maths
description: Add, take away, times and divide, and the sums games need: how many whole times something fits, and what's left over.

title: 4. Working with Text
description: Strings: join them, measure them, shout them, and put numbers inside them with f-strings.

title: 5. Making Decisions
description: if, elif and else — code that runs only sometimes, which is what makes a game react.

title: 6. Loops
description: for and while — doing something again and again without typing it again and again.

title: 7. Lists
description: Lots of values in one variable — an inventory, a high-score table — and how to loop through them.

title: 8. Functions
description: Make your own commands with def: give them inputs, and get answers back with return.

title: 9. Python in a Game
description: Variables, if and loops on the screen: draw with a loop, and grow a circle with the arrow keys.

title: 1. Player
description: A player you move with the arrow keys or WASD, who can't leave the screen.

title: 2. Gamepad
description: Play with a controller: the stick, the D-pad, and a button to run.

title: 3. Enemy
description: Enemies that fly across the screen, come back round at a random height, each at its own speed.

title: 4. Collisions
description: When the player touches an enemy, lose a life — and when the lives run out, start again.

title: 5. Score
description: A point for every enemy dodged, the score and lives on screen, and a best score that's kept.

title: 6. Time Limit
description: A 30-second countdown with an alarm, "Time's up!", and Space to play again.

title: 1. Title Screen
level: Game Elements 2: Adding to the Fun
description: A room of its own for the game's name, and a key to start playing.

title: 2. Collecting
level: Game Elements 2: Adding to the Fun
description: Coins worth 5 points that turn up somewhere new, and your first function in a script of its own.

title: 3. Projectile
level: Game Elements 2: Adding to the Fun
description: Fire bullets while Space is held, tidy them away off screen, and knock enemies back.

title: 4. Increasing Difficulty
level: Game Elements 2: Adding to the Fun
description: Enemies that speed up every time they come round — up to a limit — and more of them as time goes on.

title: 5. Multiplayer
level: Game Elements 2: Adding to the Fun
description: A second player on WASD, made from the first one with its own keys — one object defining another.

title: 6. End Screen
level: Game Elements 2: Adding to the Fun
description: A game-over room with the final score, back to the title from there, and a best score that's saved.

title: 1. Angled Movement
description: A ship that turns, and flies the way it's pointing — direction, speed, and the hspeed and vspeed they make.

title: 2. Top-Down Physics
description: Push, don't set: speed that builds up and drifts, friction to slow it, a top speed, and brakes.

title: 3. Spawning and Destroying
description: Rocks that drift, more of them on a timer, bullets made where the ship points, and both destroyed when they meet.

title: 4. Delay Timer
description: Wait before something can happen again — a rate of fire, and a moment of safety after a hit — with alarms.

title: 5. Health Bars
description: Health as a number, a bar drawn from it that changes colour, one that floats over the ship, and healing.

title: 6. Explosions
description: Effects and screen shake when a rock goes, rocks that break into smaller rocks, and sparks when the ship's hit.

title: 7. Pause Menu
description: P pauses the game; a menu of choices from a list, picked with the arrow keys and Enter.

title: 8. Button Click and Tap
description: A START button on a title screen that works with a mouse click or a tap, and lights up when you point at it.

title: 9. Level Maps
description: A new game, a platformer: its level drawn as rows of text, and loops that turn the text into walls.

title: 10. Platformer Tools
description: Walking that stops at walls, gravity, jumping only from the ground, short hops and a top falling speed.

title: 11. Scrolling Camera
description: A level three screens wide, and a camera that follows the player through it, smoothly.

title: 12. Strike and Interact
description: Slimes to fight with a sword strike that lasts a moment, and a friend to talk to when you're close.

title: Simple Platformer
description: Gravity, solid ground, running and jumping.
